newsitem.title: USA: CME lumber futures close mixed, nearby Nov lower.
newsitem.headline: CME lumber futures close mixed, nearby Nov lower.

text.p: CME lumber futures closed mixed with nearby November again pressured by concern that cash prices are falling seasonally, traders said.

Private sources put mill asking prices for spruce in the $400 to $410 per tbf area, down from the recent high of $432. Traders' bullish ideas from Thursday morning's U.S. housing starts report also appeared to be tempered as the day unfolded.
At first glance the 4.5 percent jump in starts during August to 1.525 million units was bullish to lumber. However, upon further review, the 4.4 percent decline in buliding permits was bearish.

The permit figure is a better indicator of future lumber use which kept November from filling a gap in the charts and selling ensued, traders noted. When prices fell below $355, basis November, sell stops added to the setback.

The Commerce Department reported August U.S. housing starts up 4.5 percent to 1.525 million units annually, the highest level since March 1994 when it was 1.531 million. Economists had forecast August starts at 1.445 million.
Lumber closed $1.20 per tbf lower to $6.00 higher with only November off at $350.30 and January up $1.50 at $353.70.
